emma: Observed a deterministic phase inversion in long-context runs when interleaving delta snapshots with full snapshots. Behavior shows up around token ~10.5k and only on the fast pack + reorder path.

emma: Short summary: model=nebula-14b:int8, prime_len=10500, gen_len=800. We use mixed snapshot mode (full every 5k, delta every 1k). With that cadence, outputs diverge from fp16 baseline starting at token 10498. If we switch to full-only snapshots divergence disappears.

ryan: interesting. can you paste repro and key logs?

emma: repro command:
```
MODEL=nebula-14b:int8
python -m bench.longctx_run \
  --model $MODEL \
  --prompt tests/10.5k_mixed.txt \
  --prime-len 10500 \
  --gen-len 800 \
  --snap-mode mixed_full_delta \
  --full-interval 5000 \
  --delta-interval 1000 \
  --seed 3 \
  --upload s3://redwood-debug/nebula-mixed-1778881234/
```
logs excerpt:
```
[INFO] snapshot: mode=delta idx=7 base=5 delta_size=4912
[DEBUG] packer: pack_stride=4096 pack_remainder=816
[WARN] kvcache: memcpy_mismatch expected=16384 actual=16380
[WARN] reorder: observed_reorder_count=2
[DEBUG] layer=21 token=10498 v_norm_fp16=0.923 v_norm_int8=0.914
```

juan: memcpy_mismatch=4 bytes short. pack_remainder=816 also odd (not multiple of pack_gran). Could be a reorder routine that assumes full-snapshot alignment.

emma: hypothesis: delta snapshots generate non-aligned tails; the fast reorder packs deltas into existing slot without zeroing the trailing few bytes, then full snapshot later overwrites but the transient garbage affects the intermediate KV state and seeds a phase flip that amplifies.

ryan: does the inversion always occur at the same token or does it vary?

emma: very reproducible for this prompt/seed. changing seeds shifts token but mixed cadence still triggers earlier than full-only.

juan: quick mitigation idea: when writing a delta snapshot, force-pad to slot width and append a small checksum footer so replay can detect unfilled tails. Also add a replay-verify mode that checks the snapshot against a fresh packer roundtrip.

emma: will try two experiments: (1) delta pad guard (zero-fill remainder) and (2) disable fast-reorder on deltas (software fallback). Running both on canary-05. ETA ~20m.

ci-bot: job queued: longctx-mixed-1778881234 run started; artifacts will appear at s3://redwood-ci/longctx-mixed/1778881234

ryan: also please run replay_compare with the first 6 snapshots replayed into a clean runtime and capture per-layer max-abs diffs. I pushed a small update to tools/replay_compare.py to CSV out mismatches by byte offset.

emma: running replay_compare now. Small snippet of output:
```
snapshot,layer,mode,max_abs_v,max_abs_k,byte_offset_mismatches
5,21,mixed,1.1e-03,9.8e-04,4
6,21,delta,8.9e-04,7.1e-04,0
```

juan: snapshot 5 shows byte_offset_mismatches=4 which aligns with memcpy_mismatch. Good lead.

emma: initial canary results: (a) delta pad guard -> no memcpy warnings and generation matches fp16 for this prompt up to 12k; (b) software fallback -> also matches. Uploading full logs and CSVs to s3://redwood-debug/nebula-mixed-1778881234/results/

ryan: excellent. Sounds like a simple zero-fill guard will address it. We should add a regression test that writes mixed cadence snapshots with random prompt lengths and asserts replay equality.

juan: agreed. I'll add the zero-fill plus a footer checksum and a CLI flag --delta-pad-size for operators. Also add a metric kvcache.delta_pad_applied.

emma: PR will include: unit test, pad guard, telemetry, and docs. Tagging @eng-ml and @eng-runtime for review.

ci-bot: lint OK, unit tests running for PR branch "delta-pad-guard".

ops-bot: note: rolling canary request created for nebula-14b:int8 on canary-05 and canary-06 (24h) to capture pad metric.
